test_title: PYST 73: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 24 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre A. M is a point on the circumference of the circle. If m∠MAP = 110º, then find the value of m∠MQA.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is exactly double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Here, arc PM subtends ∠MAP at the centre A and ∠MQP at point Q on the circumference.

⇒ ∠MQP = ∠MAP ÷ 2

⇒ ∠MQA = 110º ÷ 2 = 55º

**∴ The correct answer is 55º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fddcccb349e89be651a245adc5111ab7c212963fffea9bb08af968221edabe95.png] 

**Given:**

PQ is the diameter of the circle with centre A.

m∠MAP = 110º

**Concept Used:**

Angles on a straight line add up to 180º.

Angles opposite to equal sides in an isosceles triangle are equal.

The sum of all internal angles in a triangle is exactly 180º.

**Calculations:**

Since PAQ is a straight line, ∠MAP and ∠MAQ form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠MAQ = 180º − ∠MAP

⇒ ∠MAQ = 180º − 110º = 70º

In ΔMAQ, the sides AM and AQ are radii of the same circle.

⇒ AM = AQ

Since opposite angles of equal sides are equal in a triangle:

⇒ ∠AMQ = ∠MQA

The sum of all angles in ΔMAQ is 180º:

⇒ ∠MAQ + ∠AMQ + ∠MQA = 180º

⇒ 70º + 2 × ∠MQA = 180º

⇒ 2 × ∠MQA = 110º

⇒ ∠MQA = 55º

**∴ The correct answer is 55º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at the Centre Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is exactly double the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90º).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any two points on the circumference in the same segment of the circle are always equal.
